page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. The architecture excels in memory bandwidth, achieving top-tier status in cached small-block reads at 8,631.41 GB/sec and strong performance in uncached large-block reads and writes. Single-threaded and multi-threaded decompression tasks, such as bzip3, rank in the top 10%, alongside software compilation and ray tracing workloads. However, cryptographic performance and LLM inference speeds for small and medium models remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c9g.16xlarge offers high compute density and memory bandwidth per resource unit, typical of the ARMv9 architecture. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, which limits its utility for heavy storage-bound databases or large-scale deep learning training. It is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, high-throughput web serving, physics simulations, and multi-threaded data decompression.
